findings.title: Single-column CSV/TXT files load silently corrupted (delimiter sniffing splits words into columns)
findings.description: _parse_payload (hypertools/io/sources.py:744-745) reads '.csv' and '.txt' with sep=None, engine='python', which delegates delimiter detection to csv.Sniffer. For a single-column file the sniffer picks an arbitrary in-word character as the delimiter and hypertools returns a mangled DataFrame with no warning. A one-column CSV is an utterly ordinary scientific input (a list of measurements exported from anywhere). pd.read_csv's default (sep=',') handles it correctly. Extensionless single-column text files hit the same path (sources.py:774). The same sniffing also raises a raw _csv.Error on an empty .csv (see -005). Suggested fix: for '.csv' default to sep=',' (fall back to sniffing only when the comma parse yields 1 column AND another delimiter is plausible), or catch pathological sniffs.
findings.repro:
import pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
pd.DataFrame({'solo': [1, 2, 3]}).to_csv('single_col.csv', index=False)
print(hyp.load('single_col.csv'))  # WRONG: 3 columns
print(pd.read_csv('single_col.csv'))  # correct: 1 column 'solo'
findings.expected: DataFrame with shape (3, 1), single column 'solo' containing [1, 2, 3]
findings.actual:
s   l  Unnamed: 2
0  1 NaN         NaN
1  2 NaN         NaN
2  3 NaN         NaN
shape: (3, 3) columns: ['s', 'l', 'Unnamed: 2']   (sniffer chose the letter 'o' in the header 'solo' as delimiter)

findings.title: load('sotus') returns a sklearn Pipeline, not the documented State of the Union speeches (duplicate Google Drive id with nips_model)
findings.description: EXAMPLE_DATA in hypertools/io/load.py registers the SAME Google Drive file id '1J0MBhpRwdT2WChfWJ4HXYq6jU4XpyJPm' for both 'sotus' (line 24) and 'nips_model' (line 27). The hosted file for that id is a pickled sklearn Pipeline (CountVectorizer->LDA, 50 topics, pickled under sklearn 1.0.2): cached ~/hypertools_data/sotus (downloaded 2025-07-09) and ~/hypertools_data/nips_model (downloaded 2026-07-04) are byte-identical (md5 6a350ab8d85db34e7b924ac8a7f2a19b), so the id has served these bytes for at least a year. The load() docstring promises "`sotus` is a collection of State of the Union speeches from 1989-2018" but hyp.load('sotus') returns the Pipeline object (it lacks get_data(), so it passes through raw). Printing the returned object even crashes (see -004). The duplication traces to legacy master commit c3c34908 ('updated google drive file IDs'), so 0.x is equally wrong -- but 1.0 re-documents 'sotus' prominently. Consequences: (a) no way to load the actual sotus speeches; (b) it is unknowable whether the shared file is really the NIPS topic model or the SOTUS one, so 'nips_model' is also unverifiable. Fix requires re-uploading the real sotus data (and a verified nips_model) and correcting the ids.
findings.repro:
import hypertools as hyp
d = hyp.load('sotus')
print(type(d))  # sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline, not text data
import hashlib, pathlib
h = lambda p: hashlib.md5(pathlib.Path(p).expanduser().read_bytes()).hexdigest()
print(h('~/hypertools_data/sotus'), h('~/hypertools_data/nips_model'))
findings.expected: A collection of State of the Union speech texts (1989-2018), per the load() docstring
docs_impact: docs API pages generated from the load() docstring

findings.title: Unauthenticated 538 CSV download bypasses the transient-5xx retry helper
findings.description: The retry helper _github_get_with_retry exists and works (verified against a real flaky loopback server: 502,502->200 recovered on the 3rd request), and the 538 folder LISTING call routes through it (sources.py:281-283), as does the authenticated (token-present) CSV fetch (sources.py:367). But the default anonymous path fetches the actual CSV bytes via _fetch_bytes(f'{_538_RAW}/{slug}/{csv_name}') (sources.py:370), which is a plain requests.get with no retry -- so the exact transient 502/503/504 flake the helper was added for (per its own comment block, sources.py:80-84) can still fail the load at the download step for every user without a GITHUB_TOKEN, i.e. virtually all interactive users. Routing the raw.githubusercontent.com fetch through the same helper would close the gap.
findings.repro:
# code inspection: hypertools/io/sources.py:370
#   raw, _ = _fetch_bytes(f'{_538_RAW}/{slug}/{csv_name}')  # no retry
# vs listing (line 281) and authenticated fetch (line 367) which use _github_get_with_retry.
# Retry helper itself verified for real:
from hypertools.io.sources import _github_get_with_retry
# (real ThreadingHTTPServer returning 502 twice then 200 -- see phase2_network.py)
# -> ('recovered', 3)
findings.expected: All three 538 HTTP calls (listing, authenticated CSV fetch, anonymous raw CSV fetch) retry transient 502/503/504
findings.actual: Anonymous CSV fetch is a single-shot requests.get inside _fetch_bytes; a transient 502 there raises through pd.read_csv wrapping into the load failure

findings.title: repr() of every hosted *_model pipeline crashes under the shipped sklearn (notebook display raises AttributeError)
findings.description: The hosted wiki_model/sotus_model/nips_model files were pickled under scikit-learn 1.0.2; the repo venv runs 1.8.0. Unpickling emits InconsistentVersionWarning, transform() still works (returns (1, 50) topic vectors), but repr() -- what Jupyter calls when a user evaluates `hyp.load('wiki_model')` in a cell, the single most common first step -- raises AttributeError: 'Pipeline' object has no attribute 'transform_input'. Since these are hypertools-hosted artifacts documented in the load() docstring ('wiki_model is a sklearn Pipeline ... can be used to transform text to topic vectors'), the models should be re-pickled under a modern sklearn (or converted to a version-stable format) before release.

m = hyp.load('wiki_model')
print(m)  # AttributeError
findings.expected: Pipeline repr prints (as any sklearn estimator); no crash on display
findings.actual:
AttributeError: 'Pipeline' object has no attribute 'transform_input'
(raised from sklearn/utils/_pprint.py -> pipeline.get_params during repr; transform() itself works: output shape (1, 50))

findings.title: Local-file parse failures escape as cryptic internal errors (empty CSV, unknown binary, gzipped CSV)
findings.description: When a local file's content can't be parsed, the user gets a raw internal exception with no filename, no format context, and no remedy: (a) empty .csv -> _csv.Error: 'Could not determine delimiter' (from the sniffer, see -001); (b) unrecognized binary bytes fall through _parse_payload's chain to the last-resort unpickle and raise _pickle.UnpicklingError: "invalid load key, '\\x00'."; (c) a gzip-compressed 'data.csv.gz' -- a very common scientific artifact -- has suffix '.gz', matches no extension branch, fails utf-8 decode, and dies as UnpicklingError: "invalid load key, '\\x1f'." (the gzip magic byte) with no mention of compression. All three should be wrapped in HypertoolsIOError naming the file, what was tried, and (for .gz) that compressed files should be decompressed first (or better: transparently supported, since pandas handles .csv.gz natively).
findings.expected: HypertoolsIOError naming the file and the formats attempted, with a hint (e.g. 'file is empty', 'looks gzip-compressed -- decompress first')
findings.actual:
empty.csv -> Error Could not determine delimiter
t.csv.gz -> UnpicklingError invalid load key, '\x1f'.
binary.garbage -> UnpicklingError invalid load key, '\x00'.

findings.title: A mistyped bare filename triggers a real DNS lookup (any 'word.word' string is treated as a URL)
findings.description: _DOMAIN_RE (sources.py:51) matches any 'name.ext' string, so a typo'd local filename with no slash ('f19_missing_xyz.csv') is promoted to https://f19_missing_xyz.csv and requests actually attempts DNS resolution + connection (multiple seconds of retries) before the final error. Besides latency, the digest shows a ConnectionError paragraph for what is plainly a filename, and the filename leaks to the resolver. Consider excluding data-file extensions (.csv/.tsv/.npy/.pkl/...) from the schemeless-URL guess, or trying only real TLDs, or at least ordering the attempt message to de-emphasize it.
findings.expected: Fast failure: 'local file not found' digest without a network attempt for an obvious filename
findings.actual:
HypertoolsIOError: could not load 'f19_missing_xyz.csv'. Tried, in order:
  - ...
  - local file: not found at f19_missing_xyz.csv
  - URL (https://f19_missing_xyz.csv): ConnectionError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='f19_missing_xyz.csv', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: / (Caused by NameResolutionError(...Failed to resolve 'f19_missing_xyz.csv'...))

findings.title: Docstring claims the 538/kaggle prefixes 'never collide with another resolver', but they shadow existing local files
findings.description: load() docstring (load.py:116-118): "The 'fivethirtyeight/' and 'kaggle/' prefixes (steps 4-5) are explicit and unambiguous, so they never collide with another resolver". Verified for real: with an existing local file ./fivethirtyeight/bechdel (a csv with column 'local'), hyp.load('fivethirtyeight/bechdel') returned the REMOTE 538 dataset (1794, 15; columns year/imdb/title) -- the local file is silently shadowed because the prefix resolvers run before local-file resolution. The order is documented correctly elsewhere, but the 'never collide' sentence is false for relative local paths, and unlike the sklearn/seaborn shadowing note there is no documented escape (a leading './' does work, since './fivethirtyeight/...' fails the startswith check -- worth documenting).
findings.repro:
import os, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
os.makedirs('fivethirtyeight', exist_ok=True)
pd.DataFrame({'local': [1]}).to_csv('fivethirtyeight/bechdel', index=False)
print(hyp.load('fivethirtyeight/bechdel').columns[:3].tolist())
findings.expected: Either the local file wins, or the docstring notes that the prefixes shadow same-named relative paths and that './' forces local resolution

findings.title: Non-string dataset arguments raise raw internal TypeErrors (expandvars / dict-hash) instead of a friendly message
findings.description: hyp.load(123) / load(None) / load(3.14) raise TypeError: 'expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not int/NoneType/float' (leaked from os.path.expandvars at load.py:292); hyp.load({'a': 1}) raises TypeError: "unhashable type: 'dict'" (leaked from the EXAMPLE_DATA membership test at load.py:257). None of these mention hypertools.load or state the accepted input types (str, list/tuple of str). A one-line isinstance check at the top of load() would fix all four.

findings.title: A stale/invalid GITHUB_TOKEN env var breaks 538 loads with a 401 that never mentions the token
findings.description: _github_api_headers silently picks up GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN from the environment (sources.py:74). If the ambient token is expired/invalid (common: exported once and forgotten), the listing call returns 401 and the user gets 'GitHub API request for fivethirtyeight/data/bechdel failed with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.' -- with no hint that hypertools sent their env token, that the token is the problem, or that unsetting it (anonymous access) would work. The 403 rate-limit branch got a bespoke actionable message (sources.py:305-311); 401 deserves one too ('a GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN was found in your environment and was rejected -- unset or refresh it').
findings.repro: GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_invalid_token_for_audit python -c "import hypertools as hyp; hyp.load('fivethirtyeight/bechdel')"
findings.expected: Error mentions the environment token as the likely cause and the fix (unset/refresh)
findings.actual: HypertoolsIOError: GitHub API request for fivethirtyeight/data/bechdel failed with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

findings.title: hyp.save() ignores the file extension -- save(df, 'data.csv') writes pickle bytes into a .csv
findings.description: save() (hypertools/io/save.py:19-22) always pickles, whatever the extension: hyp.save(df, 'data.csv') produces a file starting b'\\x80\\x04' that pandas.read_csv cannot read (UnicodeDecodeError) and no other tool will open as CSV; only hyp.load gets it back (via content sniffing, despite the extension). The docstring does say 'Pickle obj to fname', but round-tripping is the documented purpose of save+load and scientists WILL write .csv/.npy expecting shareable files. Extension-aware export (.csv->to_csv, .npy->np.save, .parquet, ... with pickle as the default/fallback) would match load()'s extension-aware behavior and user expectations.
findings.repro:
import pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
df = pd.DataFrame({'a': [1, 2]})
hyp.save(df, 'lie.csv')
print(open('lie.csv', 'rb').read(2))  # b'\x80\x04'
pd.read_csv('lie.csv')  # UnicodeDecodeError
findings.expected: save(df, '*.csv') writes real CSV (or at minimum warns that a pickle is being written with a non-pickle extension)
findings.actual:
b'\x80\x04'
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 0: invalid start byte  (from pd.read_csv; hyp.load('lie.csv') round-trips only via pickle sniffing)

findings.title: 'Tried, in order' digest rough edges: URL inputs listed as local-file attempts with collapsed slashes; directories reported 'not found'; host:port schemeless URLs get no URL attempt
findings.description: Three cosmetic/clarity issues in load_source's otherwise-good failure digest: (a) for URL inputs the first attempt line reads e.g. "local file: not found at https:/raw.githubusercontent.com/..." -- the '//' collapsed to '/' by Path(), which looks like a mangled URL and confuses the report (same for 'file:/...' when a file:// URL is passed -- file:// scheme is unsupported entirely); (b) passing a directory yields "local file: not found at <dir>" although the path exists (it is a directory -- say so); (c) a schemeless host:port source ('127.0.0.1:8000/t.csv', or any 'localhost/...' host without a dot) fails _DOMAIN_RE so the digest contains NO URL attempt line at all, giving no clue that adding 'http://' fixes it.
findings.expected: Digest skips (or rephrases) the local-file line for URL-shaped input; says 'is a directory' when it is; suggests adding http:// for host:port strings
findings.actual: "- local file: not found at https:/raw.githubusercontent.com/..." ; "- local file: not found at /tmp/...data" (an existing directory); '127.0.0.1:61871/t.csv' digest ends at the local-file line with no URL attempt
